cards.text: When Jesus sees the crowds, He goes up on the mountain and sits down, and His disciples come to Him. Then He begins to teach them. Friend, when I sit down in my bakery, it's because my gold base tipped over and took me with it.

cards.question: Jesus' very first word is 'Blessed.' The first people He calls blessed are the poor in spirit. What does He say is theirs?

cards.text: Next, Jesus calls those who mourn blessed. I mourned in a junk drawer for YEARS, and the only name anybody ever gave it was "Hey, what's this thing?"

cards.question: What does Jesus promise those who mourn?
Jesus' first two lines about the poor in spirit and those who mourn are built the same way. What's the pattern?

answers.text: Who is blessed and what they'll get
What to do and what to avoid
A question and then its answer

cards.text: Then Jesus says the meek are blessed, for they will inherit the earth. Friend, I'm not even meek with my oven timer, and the timer WINS every single time.
Next, Jesus calls blessed those who hunger and thirst for righteousness. That's not a craving for cookies, friend, that's a craving for what's right.

cards.question: Jesus says those who hunger and thirst for righteousness will be ___.
Jesus calls the merciful blessed and promises them the very thing they give out.

cards.text: Then Jesus says the pure in heart are blessed. Friend, my heart is about 40 percent love and 60 percent butterscotch bits.

cards.question: What does Jesus say the pure in heart will do?

cards.text: Then Jesus calls the peacemakers blessed. Friend, I shared a junk drawer with dead batteries that argued over who had the most charge left, so I KNOW making peace is hard work.

cards.question: What does Jesus say the peacemakers will be called?

cards.text: Then Jesus calls blessed those who are persecuted because of righteousness. Doing right, getting treated wrong for it, and Jesus still says BLESSED.

cards.question: Jesus promises those persecuted because of righteousness the same thing He promised the poor in spirit.

cards.text: Then Jesus switches from 'those' to 'you': "Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of Me."

cards.question: People insult and persecute them because of Jesus. What does Jesus tell them to do?
Why does Jesus say they can rejoice when they're persecuted because of Him?

answers.text: Their reward in heaven is great
Their enemies will soon be punished

cards.question: Jesus says His listeners will be the first people ever persecuted this way.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "You are the salt of the earth." Friend, the best anybody ever called me was the dust of the drawer.
But then Jesus asks: if the salt loses its savor, how can it be made salty again? Sounds like a stamper losing its edges, friend, and you KNOW I've been there.

cards.question: What does Jesus say happens to salt that loses its savor?

answers.text: It's dried out in the sun

cards.text: Then Jesus paints a new picture: "You are the light of the world." Friend, I spent years in a dark drawer begging for one slice of kitchen light, and Jesus is talking about the WHOLE WORLD.

cards.question: Jesus says a city on a hill can be hidden if it tries hard enough.
Jesus says people don't light a lamp and put it under a basket. Where does He say they set it?

cards.text: Up on the stand, it gives light to everyone in the house. And Jesus says that in the same way, His listeners should let their light shine before men.

cards.question: When their light shines before men, what does Jesus say people will see?
When people see those good deeds, who does Jesus say they'll glorify?

cards.text: That's where we'll stop for now, and Mags would be ringing LOUD for this one. Keep that apron on, friend, because Jesus is NOT done teaching.

findings.problem: This is the first choice card, and it asks the baker to guess the second half of the first beatitude. Nothing in the earlier cards lets a baker reason that the poor in spirit get the kingdom of heaven, so the pick is luck.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to guess the wording of the promise to the pure in heart (see God). Nothing in the setup lets the baker reason to it over 'rule the nations' or 'never grow old.' It is a guess at a detail, like the 'anoint David's head' example.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to guess what the peacemakers will be called (sons of God). This is the next words of the line, and nothing earlier helps the baker reason past 'Shepherds of Israel' or 'Mighty men of valor.' Together with cards 2 and 11, most of the beatitude promise questions are word-guessing, not informed guesses.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't click. In 'the only name anybody ever gave it,' the word 'it' has no clear thing it points to: the mourning, the drawer, or Papa Dorin. The link to Jesus calling mourners 'blessed' needs explaining.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: 'The best anybody ever called me was the dust of the drawer' contradicts the backstory. His kids called him Papa, and the backstory says that's the best name he's ever been called.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: Multiple choice takes 6 of the 8 choice cards: true or false has 2 and fill in the blank has none. One type dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice takes 5 of the 8 choice cards, against 2 true or false and 1 fill in the blank. One type dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells nothing from the passage, yet it cites Matthew 5:16. The rule says a story card cites the verses it tells, but this card tells none, and the JSON format requires a verses value.
findings.question: What should a closing story card cite when it is only the 'story continues' line and retells no verse: the last verse of the stop, the verses of the stop, or something else?
